Specifically, the ACC and PFC regulate the allocation of attentional resources by enhancing the excitability of TPN neurons and suppressing the activity of DMN neurons, thereby facilitating task-relevant processing and inhibiting task-irrelevant processing. This neural mechanism is thought to be responsible for the ability to selectively focus on relevant stimuli and ignore irrelevant information.
